title: Measuring the Moon
subtitle: Marks on a real picture, a scale from a known length, and a size in kilometers
body:
Step 1 of 10 read

A real picture of the Moon

How big is a feature on the Moon, measured from a picture that has no scale of its own? You will decide what gives the Galileo picture a scale, then mark a dark plain on it and measure its width in kilometers.

This is a real picture: the Moon, photographed by NASA’s Galileo spacecraft on 7 December 1992 as it flew past the Earth on its way to Jupiter.

title: Measuring the Moon
subtitle: Marks on a real picture, a scale from a known length, and a size in kilometers
body:
Step 10 of 10 read

What you worked out

The uncertainty the tool states covers only the rounding of your marks. The softness of the Moon’s edge, the crop at the right, the diameter you assumed and the slant of the plain are not in it, so the real uncertainty is larger than the one printed. And because the picture is a display picture, its gray levels are not light: it can say where things are and how big they are, and nothing about how bright.
